question: Do the LP2-39 red-header crib differences appear elsewhere in the archived rune stream more often than expected from page-preserving shuffles?
crib_rule: Use all and only exact GP-label segmentations of the existing 20 predeclared words that produce three runes; do not select cribs by hit count.
difference: (ciphertext_index - plaintext_index) modulo 29, position by position; GP alphabet index, not prime-value subtraction.
source: Every archived LP1 and LP2 page with rune text except target LP2-39; punctuation removed; page-internal adjacent runes may cross printed row or word breaks, but never page boundaries.
search: Exact forward three-rune windows only, no reverse, rotation, gap, Atbash or wildcard; retain every source coordinate and candidate alias.
control: 2000 independent seeded within-page shuffles of rune indices, retaining each source page's length and marginal rune counts; recompute the complete all-crib search each time. Seed 330139.
statistic: Total matching windows for the union of distinct derived sequences; also distinct cribs with at least one hit. Compare observed to upper and lower null tails inclusively with plus-one correction.
positive_control: Replace the first three runes of the first source page with the first derived sequence and verify its hit is recovered at offset zero.
exclusions: No claim that LP2-39 red runes have any chosen plaintext; no key-layer or withheld-text validation; no prime-value differences; no other crib lists, offsets, source ordering or cipher families.
